header: Date: 2025-03-27 14:30 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (Redwood), Jordan Lee (EchoSphere), Maya Ortiz (EchoSphere), Samir Patel (EchoSphere)
summary: Initial integration discovery focused on SDKs and orchestration patterns. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for latency-sensitive retrieval-augmented generation pipelines. Key asks: LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy pattern for multitenant routing, per-route quotas/rate-limits, and observability hooks for token-level cost attribution.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript: 00:00 Alex Chen: all right everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from redwood side, i'm alex chen, i'm the AE; priya is our solutions engineer. can you all quick intro?
00:08 Jordan Lee: yeah hi i'm jordan, lead ml eng at echosphere. maya and samir are with platform and security. we're evaluating how to serve rags at scale with predictable cost and latency.
00:16 Priya Nair: great, thanks jordan. want to start high level — are you leaning hosted, dedicated, or private today? any regulatory constraints?

00:23 Maya Ortiz: we prefer hosted for speed but we have a subset of workloads (health-related PII) that may need VPC/on-prem later. right now latency is a big deal — p95 under 350 ms for short context responses is ideal.
00:35 Samir Patel: and we need audit logs and KMS integration for encryption-at-rest. SOC two compliance is a must for the pilot stage.
00:42 Alex Chen: totally — we can do SOC 2 plus KMS. for private we have a VPC option and on-prem packaging, usually a different SLT. priya, maybe run through SDKs and connectors?

00:51 Priya Nair: sure. Redwood SDKs cover python and node, simple REST wrappers, and we provide first-class LangChain and LlamaIndex adaptors. note, sometimes transcriptions label lamaindex as 'Lama Index' in our docs, but the adapter supports the canonical library. the LangChain chain-of-thought integrations are fairly standard — you can swap callables to our client.
01:12 Jordan Lee: how opinionated are the adapters? we have a custom retriever and an internal embedding pipeline. can we plug those in or do we need to rewrite?

01:20 Priya Nair: you can plug your retriever — the adaptor accepts a fetch_embeddings hook and a generate call. for embeddings we support batching and streaming; we also expose token usage metadata on responses so you can map tokens back to requests in your billing pipeline.

01:34 Maya Ortiz: interesting — about the gateway/proxy pattern: we have an existing API gateway (kong + apigee) and want a lightweight proxy that can do model routing (cost vs latency), per-tenant quotas, and fallback to cheaper models if capacity constrained. how do customers usually do that with redwood?

01:52 Alex Chen: common pattern is to put a small routing service in front — some customers use our Hosted API directly but run a thin gateway that annotates requests with tenant id and policy. we also have routing policies in the control plane that can do region-based and cost-based routing — fallback to quantized variants or cached prefixes to save tokens.
02:12 Jordan Lee: can the routing service call a single endpoint and have redwood handle multi-model routing or does that logic live client-side?

02:19 Priya Nair: both options. you can call a single 'router' endpoint and pass a policy id; Redwood will route to the model variant. the alternative is to implement routing in your gateway and call different model endpoints. for per-tenant quotas we expose quotas at API key and route levels — and rate limiting is enforced at the ingress. note: if you need strict per-tenant throttling we recommend dedicated capacity to avoid noisy neighbor headroom issues.
02:41 Samir Patel: how granular are quotas? e.g., per-route daily token caps and concurrent request limits?

02:47 Priya Nair: yes, per-route token caps, per-api-key qps, and burst allowances. Those can be configured in the console and via the API. we also emit webhook events when quotas approach thresholds so your gateway can circuit-break.
03:02 Jordan Lee: observability — what telemetry do we get? distributed tracing? per-token cost?

03:07 Miguel Santos: we provide request traces with model latency breakdowns, token counts (prompt/response), and per-model throughput metrics. you can export to datadog/jaeger/newrelic and we have a sample tracing hook in the sdk. the token-level cost attribution is available in the billing export and via realtime trace headers if you want to correlate traces to invoices.
03:26 Maya Ortiz: nice — can we add custom tags from our gateway (tenant id, request id) so it's in the trace?
03:31 Priya Nair: absolutely. the sdk accepts a metadata header and we surface it in traces and logs. just be careful about PII in telemetry — we recommend hashing tenant ids if necessary.
03:42 Jordan Lee: for latency — you mentioned caching, prefix cache? our RAG calls have a lot of repeated context. how does that work?

03:49 Priya Nair: prefix/KV cache reduces repeated decoding and model work for identical prompts; you can control cache TTL and eviction. combined with batching we often see a 30-50% token cost reduction for high duplication workloads.
04:04 Jordan Lee: on quantization — we have a baseline model with 8-bit quantized weights in prod, will that be supported on dedicated?

04:10 Miguel Santos: yes, dedicated supports quantized kernels and we auto-select optimized kernels per hardware. for private, there are some extra validation steps but we support 4/8-bit quant profiles depending on your model family.
04:21 Samir Patel: security question — SSO and RBAC? our org requires SAML SSO and strict role separation for who can deploy models or change routing policies.
04:30 Alex Chen: we support SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC in the console. we can restrict model rollout to specific roles and require approval flows for new private deployments.

04:40 Jordan Lee: ok budget/timeframe — we have a Q2 pilot window. primary success criteria: p95 latency under 350ms on short queries, predictable monthly spend within the pilot budget, and SOC2 + KMS in place before data onboarding.

04:56 Priya Nair: for pilots we usually spin up a small dedicated pool or hosted with reserved capacity — dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation which helps latency SLOs. hosted is fastest to get started, and we do a canary rollout and automatic fallback policies.
05:12 Maya Ortiz: curious about SDK ergonomics — do you have examples of a LangChain prompt loader that uses Redwood streaming responses?

05:20 Priya Nair: yes — we have a LangChain wrapper that exposes an async generator for tokens. i'll share a snippet after the call. small caveat: some community libs call it LongChain in transcripts, so watch for naming mismatches — but the code works with current LangChain and LlamaIndex versions.
05:37 Jordan Lee: demo request — can we run a small benchmark with our retriever and sample corpus? we'd like to test rerank latency and embedding similarity throughput.
05:44 Alex Chen: absolutely. next step: you send sample workload, we'll propose instance flavors (A100-like, H100-like) and a perf test plan. priya, miguel will run the baseline and share results.
06:00 Samir Patel: legal/procurement — any standard entitlements or data residency notes for hosted? we might need EU residency for some customers.
06:07 Alex Chen: we have region options in hosted; EU and US regions, and private on-prem options for strict residency. procurement-wise we can provide a pilot MSA with SOC 2 addendum.
06:16 Jordan Lee: what about token-level debugging in case we see hallucinations tied to prompt truncation? can we get full token traces?

06:23 Miguel Santos: yes we surface per-token logits mute? uh we don't surface logits by default, but we do provide token-level deltas and the full request/response tokens in audit logs for authorized roles. that usually helps debug prompt truncation or mis-tokenization issues.
06:40 Maya Ortiz: can the gateway do model multiplexing — e.g., send short text to a cheaper quantized model and long generative flows to a higher-context variant?

06:47 Priya Nair: yes, that's a typical routing policy. you can set size thresholds and cost bounds in the routing rules; Redwood's control plane will route accordingly and you can see cost impacts in the console.
06:58 Jordan Lee: about quotas again — we have a bursty traffic pattern. how do you recommend smoothing costs?
07:05 Alex Chen: we recommend a combination: burst pools (reserved but billed differently), autoscaling thresholds, and prefix caching. also use model quantized fallbacks for non-critical requests.
07:18 Samir Patel: one last security note — we need API keys to be short-lived and rotate via our KMS. integrations?
07:24 Alex Chen: we support short-lived tokens via our auth API and can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key wrapping. we'll share the integration guide.
07:32 Jordan Lee: sweet. any red flags or risks we should know now?
07:35 Priya Nair: main risk is mixed tenancy on shared hosted if you have strict p95 SLOs — that's where dedicated helps. also private deployments have longer lead times and validation steps.
07:45 Alex Chen: recap: EchoSphere sends sample workload and p95 target, Redwood shares pricing and SKDs/examples, schedule perf pilot. anything else?
07:55 Maya Ortiz: please include sample tracing config for datadog/jaeger and an example webhook for quota alerts.
08:02 Alex Chen: will do. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and calendar invite for pilot kickoff.
58:00 Meeting end
